headline: The US open confirms the AI sell-off as Anthropic slips and Norway's gas cuts deepen

findings.headline: Wall Street picks up Europe's AI unwind, and Anthropic is now caught in it
findings.body: Anthropic fell about 9% in its first full session, back below its $97.17 debut close, as Nvidia and AMD extended their losses, so the record listing has not revived the AI trade. Leading and lagging on Wall Street is split the same way as in Europe: AI-heavy tech is lagging while old-economy Dow names hold up. MarketWatch notes the S&P 500 is heading for its longest losing streak since 2020.

sources.label: CNBC: Anthropic stock falls amid AI sell-off as Nvidia, AMD also sink
MarketWatch: S&P 500 heads for longest losing streak since 2020

findings.headline: Norwegian gas supply tightens just as a cold snap arrives
findings.body: Equinor's Visund outage (13.2 mcm/day) has been extended to 1 January for fire repairs, and with cuts at Troll and Aasgard, Gassco data show Norwegian exports at 285.7 mcm/day against 335 mcm/day earlier this week. LSEG sees northwest European heating demand rising to 759 GWh/day next week from 528 GWh/day today, with storage at 69.8%, the lowest for the date since at least 2011. That combination means larger withdrawals from an already thin buffer heading into December.

ANSA: gas rises to 87 euro at the TTF

findings.headline: Silver breaks to a 14-month low with a December Fed hike fully priced
findings.body: Fed funds futures fully price a 25bp hike in December, with roughly a 10% chance of 50bp, and that is keeping the dollar firm and real yields high. Silver has dropped to its lowest in 14 months, hit by both the rates story and weaker industrial-demand expectations. The next tests are the flash PMIs on Monday and the Q3 GDP revision and October PCE on Wednesday, before Thanksgiving.

sources.label: FXStreet: Silver slides to fresh 14-month low amid hawkish Fed undertone
FXStreet: Week ahead, flash PMIs and PCE inflation in focus

view: Our view: the US open confirmed the day's tone rather than resetting it. With a December hike fully priced, relief probably needs a soft PCE print next week; until then AI-heavy growth and precious metals stay the laggards, while Norway's supply cuts leave European gas as the one area where the risk is to the upside going into the cold snap.
